text: Atlas always recommends dropping hidden indexes, but tells users to drop only after deciding they are unnecessary. Its hidden-index display covers the top 20 most active namespaces when the page loads, so it may omit others. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

text: Review usage over a representative application cycle before removing an apparently unused index. Percona warns specifically about monthly reporting indexes; OneUptime likewise qualifies zero-access candidates by a representative observation period. (medium confidence)

text: Hide a candidate before dropping it to test query-planning impact; if performance regresses, unhide it. A hidden index remains maintained and is immediately available when unhidden, avoiding a rebuild. (medium confidence)

text: Server restarts reset index-usage counters, and changing an index between hidden and visible also resets its $indexStats. Account for these observation-window resets when reviewing removal evidence. (medium confidence)
keywords: Atlas Performance Advisor drop-index recommendations (unused, redundant, hidden)

text: Hiding does not remove index maintenance or storage costs: hidden indexes are updated on writes and continue consuming disk space and memory. A hidden trial therefore tests query dependence rather than the resource savings from actual removal. (medium confidence)

text: Atlas Performance Advisor recommends removing unused, redundant, and hidden indexes to reduce write overhead and recover storage. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

text: Hiding a candidate removes it from query planning but retains write maintenance and storage costs. Unhiding restores availability without rebuilding the index. (medium confidence)

text: Before dropping based on usage counters, inspect every read-serving replica-set member: reads on another member can make one node appear to have an unused index. (medium confidence)

text: A zero access counter does not prove an index has no purpose: uniqueness checks and TTL expiration do not increment these read-usage counters.
